hypothesis: A new encoder creates a separate grammar-compatibility obligation. A model verdict about a path or string API cannot establish that the receiver accepts POSIX shell words, JSON text or URL encoding.
rule: For every frozen first-stage candidate, compare encoders within each original/modified input edit. Withhold newly introduced registered encoders as unknown; retain the prior semantic gate otherwise. Never replace a withheld candidate.
inputs: Exact original first-stage request payload: complete tests, input edits and source import fragments. No labels, native messages, model rationale or hidden/reference tests.
limitations: Only the fixed public Python encoder registry is checked.
This conservative gate can withhold valid cases; a withheld case is unknown, not a confirmed invalid test.
The existing quoting ambiguity motivated this development experiment. There is no held-out generalization claim.
The original historical provider and native costs remain part of the result.
